item.title: ✍️ To all who have honoured the memory of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America
item.description: To all who have honoured the memory of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America ✍️ On behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, I would like to express my gratitude to all those who have sent us messages of condolence and support in connection with the untimely passing of the Russian Ambassador to the United States Alexander Nikitich Darchiev. For the staff, for the team of the Foreign Ministry, his passing is an irreplaceable loss. In Alexander Nikitich, we have lost not only a professional of the highest caliber, a renowned expert on American affairs, and an unwavering patriot of our country, but also a dear friend, a sensitive and attentive mentor, and a colleague who was always ready to assist and lend a helping hand. Alexander Darchiev devoted his entire life to selfless service to his homeland. May his memory live on! All condolences received have been conveyed to the family and loved ones of the deceased. SERGEY RYABKOV, Deputy Foreign Minister of Russia

item.title: : Russia's Ministry of Finance On November 23, Moscow hosted the 12th Russia-China Financial Dialogue
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Finance : 🇷🇺 🇨🇳 On November 23, Moscow hosted the 12th Russia-China Financial Dialogue , co-chaired by Russia's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Anton Siluanov and China's Minister of Finance Lan Fo’an . 🤝 The Sides exchanged views on key areas of bilateral economic and fiscal cooperation . They discussed the macroeconomic situation, ways to ensure fiscal sustainability under current conditions, shared experiences in introducing modern technologies in public finance management, and outlined steps to coordinate their efforts at multilateral financial forums. 💬 Anton Siluanov , opening the meeting: Good relations between Russia and China are a valuable asset that must be further strengthened. Over the past 10 months, bilateral trade has grown to nearly $240 billion. More than 90 joint investment projects are being implemented in energy, transport, industry and high-tech sectors. Tourism, cultural and scientific exchanges are also expanding. On the sidelines of the Financial Dialogue, Anton Siluanov and Lan Fo’an also held a bilateral meeting to discuss cooperation on matters of mutual interest. 📄 Following the 12th Russia-China Financial Dialogue, a joint statement was adopted . #RussiaChina

item.content:encoded:

🎙
Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
Maria Zakharova
’s
answer to a media question
about Norway’s restrictions on entry for Russian and Belarusian athletes
(20 November 2026)
❓
Question: As of November 16, the Norwegian Government has restricted entry to the country for athletes from Russia and Belarus seeking to compete in sporting events. How would you comment on this?
💬
Maria Zakharova: In defiance of the decisions of the International Olympic Committee, the Court of Arbitration for Sport and international sports federations
, the Norwegian Government announced on November 13 that it intended to deny visas to Russians and Belarusians travelling to the country to take part in international competitions and to deport them if they arrived using Schengen visas issued by Norway or other countries.
The Norwegian authorities do not want to see professional athletes from Russia and Belarus,
including those competing under a neutral flag, on their territory until the “war in Ukraine” is over. They justify this measure by citing the close ties between Russian and Belarusian elite sport and government authorities.
We regard these unfriendly steps by Oslo as
blatant and outrageous discrimination against Russians on the grounds of their nationality.
This approach runs entirely counter to the universal international principle of “sport outside politics” and has nothing to do with sport in general, as it destroys the healthy competition inherent in it and turns established sporting competitions into an exclusive club for insiders.
❗️
We strongly condemn the shameful actions of the Norwegian authorities.
I would also like to point out that
Norway is far from the only country that allows itself to violate the fundamental principles of the international sports movement
, the Olympic Charter and the political neutrality of sport.
Other Nordic countries continue to take a hard line as well. For example, the Finlandia Trophy, a figure skating event in the ISU Grand Prix series, is being held in Helsinki on November 20 and 21. However, our athletes, who were initially invited by the organisers to compete, will be unable to attend because of restrictions recently imposed by the Finnish Government.
Given the exceptionally high skill level of Russian figure skaters, who would clearly have been in contention for medals,
their absence inevitably lowers the standard of the competition and devalues its results
.
We take the same view on other competitions where Western countries deny access to our talented athletes by creating artificial obstacles or directly and unlawfully refusing them entry. There is no doubt that these restrictions are driven primarily by
Russophobia
,
which has long reached epidemic proportions in the Nordic countries.
For its part, Russia
will continue to consistently defend the interests of its sports sector
and provide all necessary assistance to our national federations and teams.
☝️
We support the efforts of the Russian Ministry of Sport, the Russian Olympic Committee and the relevant sports federations to uphold our athletes’ legitimate right to compete in international tournaments, including through legal proceedings and, where necessary, by taking action against competition organisers who violate established rules.
The idea of preserving a clean, apolitical international sports movement is shared by the majority of countries, as reflected in the positions taken by many international federations.
Our country has been and remains a great sporting power, and any attempts to isolate it or push it out of international sport are futile and doomed to fail.

item.title: 🗓 On November 23, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held a meeting with the Moscow-based Ambassadors of
item.description: 🗓 On November 23, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held a meeting with the Moscow-based Ambassadors of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations ( #ASEAN ) Member States. The participants reviewed the results of the programme of events marking the 35th anniversary of Russia-ASEAN relations , celebrated this year. They discussed progress in implementing the decisions of the Russia-ASEAN Anniversary Summit (Kazan, June 17-18, 2026). 🤝 Both Sides expressed their shared commitment to stepping up efforts to develop new areas of cooperation . A frank exchange of views took place on the situation in the Asia-Pacific region and developments within ASEAN-centred mechanisms , including the East Asia Summit , the ASEAN Regional Forum and the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus . The participants emphasised the need to uphold the fundamental principles of equality and consensus underpinning these mechanisms, as well as their focus on practical cooperation aimed at strengthening the regional architecture of security and cooperation . The meeting took place in a traditionally friendly atmosphere. #RussiaASEAN

On November 23, Estonia’s Chargé d’Affaires a.i. in Moscow
Marek Uhtegi
was summoned
to the Russian Foreign Ministry, where he was
issued a strong protest over Estonia’s unfounded accusations against Russia
in connection with a failed arson attack on a defence industry facility near Tallinn and the Estonian government’s
subsequent decision to close border crossing points
on the Russian-Estonian border from December 1.
The Estonian diplomat was told that such hasty accusations,
entirely unsupported by evidence
, once again
expose the Estonian regime’s deeply Russophobic nature
.
Tallinn appears to have given
little serious thought
to the consequences of this move. Closing the state border will primarily
deal another blow to the Estonian economy and backfire on Tallinn itself
, as well as its EU and NATO allies.
This latest anti-Russian stunt by Estonia adds to the long list of
hostile actions
undertaken by this Baltic state over the years.
Estonia continues to actively support the Kiev regime,
covertly allowing Ukrainian drones to use its airspace to carry out attacks on northwestern Russia
, something the Russian Side has repeatedly documented with objective evidence.
☝️
The Estonian diplomat was once again warned that such provocative and extremely dangerous actions are
on the brink of triggering an open war with Russia.
Estonia’s hostile actions do not end there.
Tallinn is attempting to obstruct the movement of Russian cargo vessels in the Baltic Sea
, seeking to inspect, seize and detain them with the aim of imposing a naval blockade on our country.
In October, Estonia introduced
a complete ban on the transit of Russian and Belarusian grain
through its territory.
Estonia is stepping up
repressive measures against Russian-speaking and dissenting residents
who refuse to blindly follow the authorities’ official narratives aimed at comprehensively vilifying Russia.
To resolve the so-called
"Russian question"
, Tallinn has resorted not only to
banning the Russian language at all levels
, but also to criminal prosecution and deportation of those who sympathise with our country and seek to preserve their right to access their native language and culture.
In pursuing their police-state methods, the authorities do not even shy away from
coercive measures and threats to dissolve the Estonian Orthodox Christian Church
altogether.
The head of the Estonian diplomatic mission was informed that this unjustified policy of
fostering all-encompassing hostility towards our country
will continue to destabilise the situation in the region and adversely affect
both the well-being of Estonia’s residents
and
the already dire economic situation in this Baltic state
.
❗️
During the meeting, it was emphasised that
Russia reserves the right to take a comprehensive range of political and diplomatic measures
to protect its national interests and the legitimate rights of Russian citizens.

🗓
On November 23, Russia's Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
held a meeting
with
Patriarch John X of Antioch and All the East
, who is in Moscow to attend events marking
the 80th birthday of Patriarch Kirill of Moscow and All Russia
.
They exchanged views on the situation in the Middle East,
with a focus on the Christians living there.
Russia
reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with the Orthodox Church of Antioch on a range of issues
and its readiness to provide Christian communities with the assistance they need as the military and political situation deteriorates in their historic homelands.
☝️
They also discussed
the Western-inspired church schism in Ukraine
and
the ongoing persecution
of the canonical Ukrainian Orthodox Church.
***
🎙
Sergey Lavrov's
opening remarks
:
💬
We are pleased to see you, especially at a time when your See is at the heart of
major developments in the Middle East
.
In Syria, efforts to bring the nation together continue. We very much hope that, despite numerous provocations,
genuine national unity can be achieved
with the participation of all ethnic and religious communities.
In Lebanon,
the situation remains deeply worrying and shows no sign of improvement.
Much to our regret, the Israeli army’s continued operations are increasing the risk of another military confrontation, which we want to do everything we can to avoid. We believe it is essential to
preserve the structure of the Lebanese state
and safeguard the delicate balance among its three main communities.
In
our discussions
with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa,
we have welcomed his commitment to a similarly inclusive approach.
One example is the formation of the People’s Assembly, where Orthodox Christians serve, including in leadership positions. Orthodox Christians are also represented in the Government of Syria.
🤝
Your Beatitude,
we greatly value the efforts of your Church and your Patriarchate to foster unity across the region
and preserve its historical roots.
I would welcome your assessment of the situation and any ideas we could actively support
to help restore stability throughout the region
.
